answer: Each sable must be bound in the opal to a hardware enclave key, and the opal admits one sable per chip, ever. It also groups chips by the host network that attests them, and the k-th sable from one host network burns 2^k cipher. A farm of a thousand clones cannot share chips or one datacenter, so it must buy a thousand physical machines on unrelated networks, each costlier as clean hosts run out. It breaks if enclave keys can be extracted and copied.
